quest.title: Special Operation
quest.description: Grand Master Varka has returned from Amsvartnir and helped to devise a battle plan. To face the "Rächer of Solnari," the people of Nod-Krai must unite as never before...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1725, Primogem x30, Mora x76200, Hero's Wit x7, Mystic Enhancement Ore x14

chapter.num: Song of the Welkin Moon: Act III
chapter.title: A Nation That Doesn't Exist

talks.objective: Head to the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau
Head to the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau

dialogues.speaker: Fevroniya
dialogues.text: Lady Damselette... Wait, and you two? What are you doing at the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau?

dialogues.speaker: Fevroniya
dialogues.text: We've been doing our best to mind our own business lately, but if you're just gonna waltz up here like this, you're seriously pressing your luck. Don't blame us for doing what we have to.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmph! You really think that's gonna scare us off?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: We're not looking for any trouble. I just want to see Sandrone...

dialogues.speaker: Ozerov
dialogues.text: ...Do I need to remind you that you're still a wanted fugitive for deserting us?

dialogues.speaker: Ozerov
dialogues.text: Out of consideration for our former ties and the crisis we're all up against, we'll let you leave in one piece. But don't even think about trying to get insi—

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Let them in.

dialogues.speaker: Fevroniya
dialogues.text: But...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Are you going to make me repeat that?

dialogues.speaker: Fevroniya
dialogues.text: N—No, my Lady...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Sandrone seems to be in a good mood. Must be maintenance day.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: So, tell me. To what do I owe the honor this time?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: ...Actually, before you answer that... Just so we're clear — we're not colleagues anymore, Columbina. I don't owe you anything.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I promise it's nothing big.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: It seems like you've gotten the wrong idea here. The only reason I let you in was because I was bored. It seemed like a way to kill some time and satisfy my own curiosity.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Whatever miscalculations I may or may not have made in the past, I haven't lost the plot enough to even consider sticking my neck out for your sakes.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I'd like to speak with Arlecchino.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: ...What?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? You mean, The Knave!?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I'd like to speak with Arlecchino. Is she in Nod-Krai?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: No, she's not. Once the work on this facility was completed, she went back with "The Rooster" and "Regrator." The only ones in Nod-Krai now are me, and... Ahem, what is it you need to speak to her about, anyway?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Rerir is hunting me. If I'm going to face him, I must first retrieve the lost moon.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Marionette seems lost in thought, but she doesn't look surprised. She must know more than she was letting on.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I don't understand what Arlecchino has to do with the Iridescent Moon's marrow... But at this point, I have no choice but to go along with Columbina's plan.)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Is that a no, then?

choices.text: We're only doing this to stop Rerir.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Hmph, as if I need reminding. I was THIS close to settling things with him before SOMEONE decided to whisk me away to their weird little garden.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Have you held any tea parties lately?

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Tea parties? Uh, yeah, obviously. You don't seriously think we'd pack it all in just because you aren't here?

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: If anything, they've been more eventful than ever. Just me, Arlecchino, and a bunch of insolent, insensitive "guests" who won't stop asking where you've gone. Oh, they've been a real joy.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: I bet you served them the worst tea you have. Just like you used to do to me when I upset you.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Hmph... Who cares about how good the tea is when there's no one around to drink it? I keep losing people...

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: First Rosalyne, now you... I'm running out of people who can make me laugh. Honestly, what could be more ridiculous than a multi-centenarian goddess who's only ever had the plain herbal tea she received as offerings? Heh...

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: You'd always brew a different type of tea for me each time. Was it really just to see how I'd react?

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: I, uh— Well, duh! Why else? Watching you squirm was practically my only form of entertainment.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Or was she genuinely trying to introduce Columbina to new flavors? Maybe all that coldness is just an act... and they actually get along?)

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Oh, yeah... and Capitano sometimes used to bring Tartaglia around too, but I guess we won't be seeing him again.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Hmph... Well, I guess we are overdue for a get-together. Pulonia!

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Have Fevroniya pass a message to Arlecchino for me. "It's time for tea" will suffice.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Pass along a message for me too, if you would: "My body cannot contain the marrow of two moons, so I'll be leaving one of them in her care."

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Excuse me? Who said you were on the guest list? If my tea meant that much to you, maybe quitting the Fatui wasn't your brightest move.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Back when you were under the Tsaritsa's protection, no one would have dared come at you so openly.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: But that protection didn't come for free — in fact, I paid dearly for it. At the end of the day, it was just another transaction.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: I just got tired, that's all... I never wanted any part in their grand ambitions, and I've had enough of being treated like a bottomless supply of power.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: It brings back memories from the old days, when I was still worshiped as the Moon Goddess. Centuries on, it may be a different group of people, but I see the same greed in their eyes.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Hmph... I figured you'd leave eventually. You didn't have as much of a reason to stay as I do.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: The Tsaritsa gave you shelter and protection, but that was it — nothing more, nothing less. Meanwhile, the Fatui demanded everything from you in return, until it was more than you could bear.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: I get why you left. And frankly, I have no interest in dragging you back just because the higher-ups told me to.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: But if you keep hanging around with this riffraff, the next time we cross paths, we might be enemies for real.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (She says that, but she's the one who just caved in and agreed to help Columbina...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Heh... Well, uh... Guess that's our cue to leave?

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Umm... That might be your plan, but it sounds like someone else wants you to stay a little longer.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? What do you mean?

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: See for yourselves.

response.speaker: The Wild Hunt's Roar
response.text: Raargh!

response.speaker: Ozerov
response.text: My Lady, it's the Wild Hunt! A horde of monsters is headed straight for the facility!

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Ugh. Another uninvited guest trying to crash my tea party. Clear the area — I'll handle this.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, what? You want us to leave you here by yourself?

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Heh, you'll be lucky to make it out of this alive. You really think you can afford to worry about me?

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Go on, get out of here! You may have stopped Pulonia from crushing him last time, but I've made sure that won't happen again. The entire Experimental Design Bureau is rigged for war!

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Stay and watch if you want — but it'll be at your own risk. You're not flagged as friendlies in the weapon system.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Just... be careful, okay?

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Don't tell me what to do! Look, if you're leaving, make it quick, or you'll just get in my way. There's a secret passage on the second floor — it'll take you right to the plains out back.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Stare all you want, Columbina. You're not getting another invitation to my tea party.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: I know... But thank you anyway, Sandrone.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Ugh... This is exactly why you shouldn't hang around with those people. All their melodrama and sentimental nonsense is rubbing off on you.

choices.text: We'd better not keep Varka and the others waiting.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Come on then, Mr. Rächer. Let's pick up where we left off.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: It's your Wild Hunt monstrosities versus my beautiful creations... Let's see who comes out on top!

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: Hmph...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Pulonia, get him!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: I've upgraded Pulonia again since our last encounter... and uploaded every last scrap of your data. So let's finish this, once and for—

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: She's not here...

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: Where did she go?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Hey, over here, you big—

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: Cursed... moon...

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: Go... Keep searching. She cannot have gotten far.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: So this is your method for investigating Rerir's past? It almost looks like some kind of... ceremony.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Good deduction. But it's quite a different affair from what you're used to with the Frostmoon Scions.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: (Whoa... First time I've ever been in here. Boss always said it was off-limits, so I pictured some kind of creepy dungeon... But it's actually kinda nice!)

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: (Oh! I guess this must be Sumeru decor? That's where boss is from... and that nice shopkeeper who sold me my treasure compass.)

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I'm not sure exactly what you've got planned, but it looks like you're all set. When do we begin?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Whenever we wish... But for some reason, I've got a feeling this isn't going to end well.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I've never faced Rerir myself. But from what you've told me, his power is beyond anything I could imagine.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I, on the other hand, am just an ordinary businesswoman. Our paths should never have crossed, yet here I am, forced to make an enemy of him.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: If you ask me, you're about as far from "ordinary" as it gets. So what are you saying? You're getting cold feet?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Once I take a job, there's no backing out. Still... I have to ask myself if the power I'm relying on will even work on an opponent of this caliber.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: ...And also, how to make sure I come out of this alive if things spiral out of control.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Death is the one thing we can take for granted. It is the great equalizer, however fortunate or unfortunate we may otherwise be. So it's important to consider how to spend what lifespan we have left.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Haha... C'mon boss, lighten up. Quit talking about death, it's bad luck!

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: ...For once, I agree with you. When you're up against a foe like Rerir, there's no such thing as being too prepared.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Is there anything I can do to help?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: That won't be necessary. I've already made up my mind... Time to cash in a precious favor I've been saving for a rainy day. Jahoda, I need you to find someone for me — the sooner, the better.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Eh? Find who?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: That shady merchant who sold you an overpriced treasure compass the other day.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Come on, boss, you're pulling my leg again! In what way is she shady? She showed up when I was completely lost and sold me a neat little gadget that was exactly what I needed! Trust me, she's a good person!

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Anyway, I know who you're talking about. Don't go anywhere, I'll be right back!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: A few moments later...
*panting* ...Quit dragging me, I genuinely can't run any further!

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Hey, aren't you...

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: What is it? What's the big rush? You dragged me out of a dream where I was literally swimming in Mora... I—I'm charging double my usual attendance fee!

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: (See? Look how easygoing she is! After that rude awakening, she could've completely snapped at us, but instead she kept it together and just asked for an extra fee.)

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Dori Sangemah Bay? I never would've pictured you two doing business together.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: If you wanna make it big in Nod-Krai, it's all about connections. Lady Nefer just so happens to have a lot of intel that interests me — and she also did me a big favor in the past.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: It was back when I first arrived in Nod-Krai. My trusty assistant, the Jinni in my lamp, had an adverse reaction to the kuuvahki and fainted.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: And wouldn't you know it, that's when I suddenly find myself in a life-or-death situation. Good thing my compatriot was there to swoop in and save the day.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: I've been giving her a thirty percent discount off all of my goods ever since. Now, so that no one here feels left out, I'm willing to extend a twenty percent discount to fellow friends of Boss Nefer.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Plus, any other friends you send my way will enjoy ten percent off. What can I say? The great Lord Sangemah Bay is nothing if not generous...

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: So, let me guess... You've run into some trouble? Hehe, I've got everything you could possibly need — and the more you buy, the more you'll save.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: You guessed correctly. What have you got in the way of survival gear?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Heh, the one type of gear I've never been short on! What are you looking for? A jetpack fresh from the Akademiya's labs? An ancient suit of armor, dredged up from the bottom of the sea?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: At the very least, I need to know what kind of opponent you're dealing with here. If even you're worried about staying alive, it must be pretty serious...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: What if I told you it's someone with the power to bring a nation to its knees?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Is that so? Hmm... Then we really are talking top-shelf treasures. I don't have anything like that in stock right now... I'll have to ask my supplier.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Your supplier?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: A powerful woman, make no mistake... I can't reveal her identity, but luckily for you, I hear she's planning to visit Nod-Krai in the near future.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: If you're willing to wait, I can ask her once she's here. Can't say exactly how long that'll be, though...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Then let me put it another way... What would you do if you encountered an enemy like that? Roll over and serve yourself up on a silver platter?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Course not! I have a handy little trinket from one of my generous suppliers, which... Hold on, what exactly are you getting at? No, no, this is for my personal use only!

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Let's just say I'm borrowing it, alright? Just for insurance purposes — you'll get it back later.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Favors are the worst kind of debt to owe, and now you've got a chance to repay one. A win-win situation, don't you think?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: ...Hmph, fine. You can borrow it for five days... No, make that three! And for every extra hour after that, I'm charging you a million Mora. Deal?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Deal.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: *sigh* What a way to start the day... Now, was there anything else you wanted, or can I go back to bed now?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: That will be all. Take care, now — don't trip up on your way back, friend.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: See you later! You're my favorite shopkeeper!

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Excellent, everything is well and truly ready. The ceremony can now begin.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: After initiating the ceremony, your minds will follow me wherever I go. You will see many strange things in your mind's eye.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: So remember: Don't be frightened, and don't make a sound...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After laying down the ground rules for everyone who will be joining the trip as a follower, Nefer begins the ceremony.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Now then... Let us peer into the Rächer of Solnari's past.

dialogues.speaker: Check
dialogues.text: A few storage boxes sit next to the cabinet. Everything in sight is neatly organized.

dialogues.speaker: Check
dialogues.text: Whoever lives here seems to be enjoying a pretty comfortable life.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (...I made it.)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (I don't recognize this style of architecture... Must be Khaenri'ahn.)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (Simple furnishings, table and chairs... It's a more ordinary house than I might have expected.)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (...Looks like the fearsome "Rächer of Solnari" came from surprisingly humble beginnings.)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (Unless this passed for luxury in Khaenri'ah...? Hmm, unlikely. It was said to be a very prosperous nation in its heyday.)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (...Anyway. I'll keep exploring.)

talks.objective: Investigate the note on the table

dialogues.speaker: A Note
dialogues.text: A handwritten note.

dialogues.speaker: A Note
dialogues.text: Hi, Rerir. Since you're working extra hours tonight, I thought I'd keep myself busy by checking out that new kebab shop. I've heard good things about their menu.

dialogues.speaker: A Note
dialogues.text: I'll test it out, and if it's as good as everyone's saying, let's go back together some time.

dialogues.speaker: A Note
dialogues.text: (P.S.: New stash from the Universitas Magistrorum. I brought some goodies home — a few teacups and a pen rack. Hope you like them!)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (They didn't sign their name... But they must have been close. Sounds like they were living together.)

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Rerir! Over here!

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Dain! Oh, and... Vedrfolnir? What a surprise to see you here, Sir.

dialogues.speaker: Vedrfolnir
dialogues.text: Hello there, Rerir. You need not address me so formally outside of court.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: He doesn't get much free time, so I invited him over for a drink. Even the court prophet deserves a break every now and then, right?

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Haha, well, I'm flattered.

dialogues.speaker: Vedrfolnir
dialogues.text: So... What are we discussing today?

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Hey, don't look at me. As far as I see it, we don't need an excuse to have a few drinks.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Come on, don't give us that! Didn't you say you were about to pop the big question? How's that coming along?

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Heh, who'd have thought the great Twilight Sword was an even greater gossip?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: I just didn't expect you to be the first one to settle down and get married, that's all.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Yeah... If you'd told me that a few years ago, I wouldn't have believed you either. Haha...

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: So, are you planning to come clean about your job, then? I'm guessing you still haven't told her.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Sure, I'll have to tell her at some point... but I'll need to pick the right time and place. To be honest, I have no idea how she'll take it.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Come on, stop being such a pessimist. For all you know, she could be thrilled! I bet she'll be much more impressed by your actual job than the one she thinks you're doing now.

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: A member of the "King's Guard"... Heh, quite the cover story. Does the king himself even know?

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Of course he does. Anyway, enough about me. How've you been?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: Me? Same old, same old, nothing much to— Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Dainsleif
dialogues.text: What's up, Ved?

dialogues.speaker: Vedrfolnir
dialogues.text: ...It's nothing.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: (Vedrfolnir, Dainsleif's elder brother... Renowned throughout the Court of Khaenri'ah as "The Visionary," and said to possess a wisdom far beyond the reach of any ordinary man.)

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: (And yet, despite the gulf between us, he seems to have something to say about me...)

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: (Does he even know me? Does he see me as a friend of his brother... or just another of the Vinster King's blades?)

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: (Why did he react so strongly? Was it really to do with what we were talking about?)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (Brown, curly hair, and brooding blue eyes. So this is what Rerir looked like back in the day.)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (Perfectly normal, no different from anyone else.)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (As frightening as this monster is in the present... There's something even more unsettling about seeing the human he used to be.)

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Tholindis? You're back early.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: Our equipment's being serviced today, so I got off earlier than usual. How's your day been?

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: Aw, why the long face? Is something the matter? Has your boss been giving you a hard time again?

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Went for a drink with Dain and the others after work.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: Isn't that a good thing?

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Vedrfolnir showed up today too. You know, Dainsleif's older brother.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: Ah, Mr. Vedrfolnir. Yes, I've heard of him. They say that everything he says ends up coming true.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: ...He overheard Dainsleif mention that I'd recently proposed, and seemed to have an issue with it. But when I asked what it was, he kept it to himself.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: So... you're worried? You can be such a child sometimes, Rerir.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: We're nobodies. Why would The Visionary be concerned about us?

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: I'm sure someone in his position has much bigger fish to fry.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Ha... Maybe you're right.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: You worry too much, Rerir. We've been together for ages now, and everything's been going so well, has it not? You've even proposed to me!

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Haha, so you do remember. Tell me, then... what's your answer?

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: Like I said, I need some time to decide. You can't just rush into things like this. We may be nobodies in the grand scheme of things, but if we want things to work out, we've still got to plan ahead.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Alright, take your time. Just don't keep me waiting forever.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: ("Nobodies"... Hmph, sounds about right. In the eyes of people like Vedrfolnir and Dainsleif, what do we matter?)

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: (Can someone whose gaze is so fixed on the far-flung future even see the present clearly? Besides... The dynasty's fate rests with the king and his inner circle. Whatever I do, it won't make much difference.)

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: (Meanwhile, every idea they come up with and every decision they make, it affects everything... These days, the king is lost in his research, and the purge of the Crimson Moon bloodline grows ever more intense.)

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: (The opposition tried to speak out, but nothing came of it. And I'm under no illusions as to why — because we eliminated them and got rid of their bodies.)

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: (A man can have a thousand reasons to carry a sword, but there are few good excuses to use it. Yet the king has never even considered a gentler approach, and he never will.)

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: (...What becomes of someone who kills on another's behalf? Can he ever find true peace?)

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Tholindis... I...

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: *sigh* It's nothing. You are right... Fate has never smiled upon nobodies like us. But by the same token, it's unlikely to bear a grudge against us, either.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: There's no reason we can't keep living happily together, cherishing the simple joys of each day as they come...

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: See? You just need to stay positive, Rerir.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: I can feel your warmth, your breath... You're right there, right by my side.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: Just seeing you makes me happy in a way I can't explain, and that's something that no one could ever take away from me. So smile, my love... Let go of that frown.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: You're right, Tholindis. I've just been overthinking things.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: That's better. Getting caught up about things like this will only ruin our evening. Speaking of which... All set for the ball tonight? I need to go get ready.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: You go ahead. I just have a few things to take care of, then I'll come join you.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: Even busier than the big shots, huh? Fine, I'll go get started... but don't be late. If you keep me waiting too long, I won't be a happy bunny.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Relax, I'll be there...

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Seriously, though, you drive a hard bargain... You're really gonna leave my proposal hanging, and still expect me to take you to the ball?

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: Well that goes without saying. I already told everyone I'd be coming with a dance partner.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: Besides, they're two completely different things... Let's take it one thing at a time, alright?

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Hmph...

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Alright, white outfit it is.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (It seems like Rerir was deliberately hiding his ties to the intelligence services... by giving the impression that he was just an ordinary member of the Vinster King's guard.)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (He clearly doesn't want his would-be fiancee to know about his other life. Then again, that's hardly surprising — people in the intelligence trade rarely do.)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (Heh, who'd have thought we were in the same line of work...)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (Let's dig a little deeper.)

dialogues.speaker: Thorkell
dialogues.text: Our last operation was a resounding success — and all thanks to you, Rächer of Solnari. In total, we apprehended 32 dregs of the Crimson Moon, and 67 accomplices.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: After all these years since the dynasty's fall, so many of them still linger on.

dialogues.speaker: Thorkell
dialogues.text: Indeed, it cannot be denied. Yet it was destiny that the Crimson Moon should be overcome by the Eclipse, and that His Majesty, the all-seeing Vinster King, now guides our nation on the path to prosperity.

dialogues.speaker: Thorkell
dialogues.text: Khaenri'ah has no further need for a dead moon. But alas, there will always be those who refuse to see the truth, choosing instead to romanticize the past.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: That's not entirely true. Much about the Crimson Moon era was worthy of remembrance, and that's exactly why they keep trying to see it restored.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Many of its secrets remain unsolved to this day. As it happens, that's precisely the field of study my partner is devoted to.

dialogues.speaker: Thorkell
dialogues.text: You still haven't told her what you really do for a living?

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Where would I even start?

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: How do you tell someone that you're one of the king's hand-picked executioners? That your hands are steeped in blood?

dialogues.speaker: Thorkell
dialogues.text: You didn't choose this life, any more than I did. Orphans like us don't get a say.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: But I'll sure as heck be the one to pay for it.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Speaking of which... We need to be more rigorous in the way we identify direct descendants of the Crimson Moon.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Someone, it seems, has strong opinions about my future plans — most likely my marriage, in particular. I have a feeling that we may soon become targets of the Crimson Moon's retribution.

dialogues.speaker: Thorkell
dialogues.text: Your concerns are not unfounded. They've taken out many of our colleagues these past few years, and for that very reason. These are no helpless lambs we're leading to the slaughter — they're wolves in sheep's clothing.

dialogues.speaker: Thorkell
dialogues.text: Take care, Rächer of Solnari. I look forward to toasting you at your wedding.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Thanks, Thorkell. You look after yourself too.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Tholindis, I never wanted to keep this from you. You're the last person I would ever want to lie to.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: But that's exactly why I can't tell you everything. There are things you shouldn't know... things you cannot know.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: The moonlit dynasties are a thing of the past. Yet even now, with the sun shining high in the sky, there are those who would call forth a dead moon's ghost.

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: Could that be why Vedrfolnir held back? Or was it because of some court secret he's not at liberty to share?

dialogues.speaker: Rerir
dialogues.text: ...I have to get a clear answer from him. No matter what happens, I will protect Tholindis.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (Rerir seems to be very concerned by Vedrfolnir's reaction...)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (Vedrfolnir and Dainsleif, "The Visionary" and "Twilight Sword." So that's what they were really like...)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (I've investigated this whole area now. There doesn't seem to be any other memories here.)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (Should I try somewhere else? Wait a second... What's this black smoke?)

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: So he's late, after all! Just you wait, Rerir... You're in for it, big time!

dialogues.speaker: Orlog
dialogues.text: Are you waiting for someone, Ma'am? Could I tempt you into buying some flowers?

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: Hm? Oh, sure. Pick me out a pretty bunch, if you would.

dialogues.speaker: Orlog
dialogues.text: Thank you! But I'm afraid none of them are as pretty as you...

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: For someone so young, you sure have a way with words, don't you?

dialogues.speaker: Orlog
dialogues.text: I'm only telling the truth. Look me in the eyes... you'll see I'm not lying.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: You're...

dialogues.speaker: Orlog
dialogues.text: May we have a word in private?

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: ...Who are you, and what do you want?

dialogues.speaker: Orlog
dialogues.text: It doesn't matter who I am. Too many of our kind have fallen lately, so I decided to take the risk of reaching out.

dialogues.speaker: Orlog
dialogues.text: Not long ago, the Rächer of Solnari led an assault on one of our strongholds. We suffered many casualties, and many who came to our aid lost their lives as well.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: Sorry, I don't know why you're telling me this... and I don't want to get involved.

dialogues.speaker: Orlog
dialogues.text: Wait... Hear me out. This time, we finally got a clear look at his face and learned his true identity.

dialogues.speaker: Orlog
dialogues.text: His name is Rerir, and he claims to be one of the king's guards.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: ...What did you say!?

dialogues.speaker: Orlog
dialogues.text: A cruel irony, isn't it... the man you're set to marry leads a double life as a brutal executioner. But surely, you must have caught a whiff of the blood on his hands?

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: Why are you telling me all of this now?

dialogues.speaker: Orlog
dialogues.text: Simple. It's because...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (How strange... Rerir was nowhere to be seen in that memory. It clearly belonged to Tholindis.)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (Rerir couldn't possibly know what happened if he wasn't even there.)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (Why would her memories appear in his fragment?)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (...The ceremony won't last much longer... I think it's time to call it a day.)

talks.objective: Summarize the clues you have on Rerir

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: So that was your doing? Did you just... pull us inside Rerir's fragment to spy directly on his memories?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Any more questions and I'll have to start charging.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: I had no idea you could do that, boss! Seriously, that was amazing... We're not worthy, we're not worthy!

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: I gotta admit, though, I'm itching to see what happens next... Feels like we barely scratched the surface...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I'm just as curious as you are, but the ceremony only allows for limited time inside. That's all we can see for now.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Luckily, we managed to learn quite a lot.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: So far, so good... I just hope the others are doing okay too.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: #Especially the group with {NICKNAME}... Their mission is a risky one. Let's hope it's all going smoothly.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: If you're worried about them, go see how they're doing.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: If I know Boss, she's gonna need some time to write up all the details and make sure it's all coherent. I'll stay behind to lend a hand, but feel free to head back and meet up with the others.

talks.objective: Summarize the clues you have on Rerir

dialogues.speaker: Check
dialogues.text: A mirror stands in the corner.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: (Perhaps it's a window into Rerir's past.)
